checks.note: The widest chord of a regular heptagon of radius 60 m is 2 x 60 x sin(3 pi / 7) = 117.0 m, computed from the stated radius (the paper prints no chord); the check tests the scale of the figure against the stated 60 m.
checks.quote: 7 strings in cluster are installed in the vertices of a regular heptagon with the radius of 60 m, the 8th string is installed in its center.

geometry.locator: arXiv:2309.16310 Fig. 1 right panel (top view, 2023), cluster 2; registered to arXiv:2108.00212 Fig. 2; year of deployment from the Fig. 1 left-panel legend
geometry.note: Confidence derived: positions read from published figures and placed at a coordinate rounded to a minute; relative layout about 5 m, absolute about 1500 m.

method: The eight strings of cluster 2 (one central, seven on a heptagon of 60 m radius), centre string -5 m east and +150 m north of the pattern centroid. Layout: the eight string positions of each cluster are the eight dark-green dots of that cluster in the top view (Fig. 1, right panel) of arXiv:2309.16310 (ICRC 2023), a to-scale schematic with a north arrow and a 0-100 m bar. Detected by colour (97 dots), the schematic was registered by a similarity transform onto the measured planar positions of the strings of clusters 1 to 8 plotted in Fig. 2 of arXiv:2108.00212 (axes in metres, "X is eastbound, Y is northbound"): 63 of the 64 dots of clusters 1 to 8 match a measured string within 8 m (rms 3.1 m), scale 2.58 m per pixel, rotation 0.1 deg. Clusters 1 to 11 have 8 dots each (one spurious detection at cluster 5 removed); clusters 12 and 13 are drawn incomplete in that figure (5 and 2 or 3 dots) and clusters 14 to 16 have no top view, so they are not drawn. Within a cluster the seven outer strings lie 58 m to 62 m from the central one (stated: "a regular heptagon with the radius of 60 m"). The schematic is idealised and the measured 2021 positions scatter by up to about 6 m about the ideal heptagon, so strings are good to about 5 m relative to each other. The two source frames have no stated origin. Placement: the centroid of the eleven central strings is put at the published site coordinate, 51 46' N, 104 24' E (arXiv:2309.16310, 2412.00164, 2507.01893; rounded to a minute), in an azimuthal-equidistant projection (WGS 84) with the figure's north up. That coordinate is not defined as a cluster, so the pattern as a whole is only good to about 1500 m: a minute of latitude is 1.85 km, a minute of longitude 1.15 km, the point could be any cluster or the field centre, and a 2013 paper gives 51 50' N, 104 20' E, 8.7 km away. Each string is a 1 m square position marker (a string anchor on the lakebed is a few metres across at most; size symbolic).
name: Baikal-GVD cluster 2 (deployed 2017)
notes: Year of deployment from the legend of Fig. 1 (left panel) of arXiv:2309.16310: 1: 2016, 2: 2017, 3: 2018, 4 and 5: 2019, 6 and 7: 2020, 8: 2021, 9 and 10: 2022, 11 and 12: 2023, 13: experimental.
Licence note: arXiv:2309.16310 and arXiv:2108.00212 are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Only positions (facts) were read from their figures; no image is reproduced.

summary.plain: One of the Baikal-GVD clusters (8 strings, 36 sensors each) on the Lake Baikal bed, deployed in 2017; drawn at its published position relative to the other clusters, with the whole field good to about 1.5 km.
